Quick triage notes (initial):
- Preliminary signal: tail latency increases correlate strongly with model v3 canary instances serving longer-sequence requests. KV cache miss rate jumps on those nodes.
- We see a change in kernel selection path (quantized path) under certain sequence-length distributions that increases per-token compute for some shards.
- Suggested immediate mitigations:
  1) Redirect 100% of Sentinel traffic to the v2 variant (instant rollback at routing layer).
  2) Increase target batch size on v3 nodes to amortize per-token cost (temporary).
  3) Enable strict short-sequence routing policy for customer until we stabilize.

I can implement #1 and #3 in the next 10 minutes if we have approval. If the customer prefers, we can do a canary rollback (stop traffic to v3) now and investigate deeper.

Subject: Re: Production spike: p95/p99 up and throughput drop during model v3 canary

Root cause (quick, from canary telemetry):
- On v3 instances we observed a bimodal sequence-length distribution from Sentinel traffic (many long prompts plus short ones). Long sequences are causing earlier KV eviction and forcing repeated recomputation for attention kernels. Under the current quantized kernel selection, that yields a ~3-4x increase in tail per-token time for affected batches.
- Memory pressure pattern: GC-like spikes that align with the p99 windows.

Short term plan I executed:
- Shifted Sentinel routing to v2 variant (rolled back canary traffic) at 09:50 PDT — this cut p95 down to ~140ms and p99 below 400ms for the sample window.
- Collected traces and generated p99_report.csv (attached) and a short server log bundle.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Keep Sentinel on v2 while we push a micro-patch to the v3 runtime that adjusts kernel selection heuristics and increases KV cache thresholds.
2) Re-run canary for a small fraction of traffic once patch is validated.

I'll prepare a patch PR and a staged rollout plan. We should avoid a full rollback across customers — this looks workload-specific (sequence-length distribution).

-Jonas
